title: Effectiveness of Reintroduction and Habitat Management Actions on the Valcheta Frog (Pleurodema somuncurense) in the Valcheta Stream, Northern Patagonia, Argentina
content:
ABSTRACT

The Valcheta Frog (Pleurodema somuncurense) is a Critically Endangered microendemic amphibian confined to the thermal headwaters of Valcheta Stream in Patagonia, Argentina. Populations of this freshwater species have declined due to invasive trout and livestock-driven habitat degradation. We evaluated habitat restoration (livestock exclusion, microhabitat enhancement) and captive-bred reintroductions by analysing demographic parameters across four reintroduced and one wild population. From December 2023 to March 2024, we conducted capture–mark–recapture (CMR), marking 456 individuals (55% adults; 45% juveniles) to estimate survival, density and recruitment using POPAN in MARK. We examined microhabitat variables (vegetation cover, rock shelters, water temperature, water velocity) and release effort via Monte Carlo linear models. Juveniles exhibited lower survival than adults; densities varied from zero at Cora to maxima at Piletones and Rincón; recruitment ranged from 3.1 juveniles per adult at Rincón (95% CI: 2.5–3.8) to 0.1 at Destacamento (95% CI: 0.1–0.4). Density correlated positively with rock shelter availability (R2 = 0.53, p = 0.007), and juvenile survival increased with summer temperature (R2 = 0.97, p = 0.01). Release cohort size did not predict density (p > 0.1). These results indicate that microhabitat quality and environmental suitability, rather than release numbers alone, drive success in reintroduction. Effective conservation of P. somuncurense therefore requires rigorous habitat assessment, passive restoration through livestock exclusion and targeted microhabitat enhancements to support all life stages.
